I still use that powdered detergent, the one in the big orange box, because the liquid stuff just gets everywhere and leaves a terrible sticky ring on the washing machine lid. Arthur used to just throw everything in together on whatever temperature the dial was stuck on—drove me absolutely up the wall, bless his heart. But I have my system. And I do my own grocery shopping, I cook my own meals... like that baked cod I mentioned, and I make a wonderful roasted chicken on Sundays with carrots and those little red potatoes, the waxy ones that hold their shape in the oven. 

I keep the house spotless, too. Now, I might... well, I might misplace the feather duster for twenty minutes while I'm in the middle of doing it, mind you, and I might eventually find it sitting on top of the refrigerator for some completely inexplicable reason, but I still get the dusting done all by myself! I don't need a home aide or my nephew Steven coming over to babysit me. I'm only 63, after all. I can still manage my own life and my own house just fine. It's really just the losing things that's the bother, the... the objects themselves wandering off, as it feels. But the actual doing of the daily tasks? No, I don't need a lick of help with any of that.

symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient explicitly states that 'losing things' is a bother and gives an example of misplacing a feather duster and finding it on the refrigerator.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
